pairwiseMatch.question: which game matches the sentence better (blind, sides by pure-rand seed 45045 per batch)

pairs.why: Both games show a fish swimming underwater through gaps between upper and lower obstacles. Game A’s solid green pipe-like barriers more clearly reproduce Flappy Bird’s defining obstacle course, while Game B uses stacks of coral-like objects.

Game B shows an armored space marine firing across red alien terrain toward bug-like creatures, with industrial towers and machinery suggesting a mining colony. Game A also shows an armored shooter and small creatures, but its hazy skyline and scattered crates make the space-colony setting less clear.

Both games show a sparse shopping area with storefronts, kiosks, and aiming reticles, though neither clearly looks like an indoor mall. Game B more clearly shows shooting at approaching humanoid enemies with health bars, while Game A mostly shows the player aiming across an empty scene.

Both games show a snowy field with an igloo, small distant characters, and projectiles thrown toward them, but neither clearly shows kids sheltering behind a snow fort. Game A has a larger igloo, while Game B adds foreground snowmen; neither difference improves the match.

Both games show an orange hamster fleeing a large black-and-red Roomba along an aisle filled with groceries, shopping carts, and supermarket shelves. The characters, setting, and escape action appear equivalent in both.

Both games show a banana running ahead of a monkey along a path with obstacles and collectibles. Game B’s stone towers and ruins better match Temple Run’s setting, while Game A runs through green countryside with windmills.

Game A shows an obstacle course of dark platforms over glowing lava, with volcanoes and bars across the route. Game B shows sandy platforms over blue water among palm trees, so it matches the lava setting much less closely.

Game A shows a boat racing along a teal river through dense jungle with crocodile-like creatures beside the course. Game B has similar boats and jungle scenery, but its brown course looks more like a dirt track than a river.

Game B shows colored gem-like pieces on tiles inside a rocky cave, with groups sparkling and disappearing, closer to Candy Crush’s matching action. Game A shows fruit-like objects falling into a tall bin beneath a crystal, with little visible matching or cave setting.

Game B shows a cat-shaped launcher facing stacks of brown cardboard-like boxes with small cat figures, better matching Angry Birds-style target destruction. Game A has a similar launcher and grassy setting, but mostly scattered small targets and floating robot-like enemies, with no clear box structures.

Game A shows a horizontal wooden log as the target, with knives flying toward it. Game B shows a similar throwing scene, but its target looks like a vertical stack of colorful blocks rather than a spinning log.

Both games show a black vortex moving through a paved city area with cars, trees, and street furniture. In A, the vortex becomes visibly larger over time; B’s stays relatively small and more prominently encounters red robots, making A better match growth through swallowing the city.
